docket.challenge_claim: That the no-scene-shift clause is contested by an explicit temporal frame and a separate divine-speech onset at 13:6 the enumeration passes over, that the 13:1 formula carries a form label the pointed bytes do not support, and that 13:3's onset is asserted without a pointed splice while 13:8's is spliced.
docket.grounds: All three arms hold, at low weight. oshb:Jer.13.6 opens וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים and then carries the separate divine-speech onset וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י (both byte), commanding a second journey to the river -- an explicit time-and-place transition standing inside the span, so the clause that no addressee or scene shift interrupts the sequence overstates what the bytes carry. The form label fails on the bytes: אָמַ֨ר at oshb:Jer.13.1 (byte) is a suffix-conjugation form, while the narrative wayyiqtol shapes of this span stand at 13:3, 13:6, 13:7 and 13:8 -- so the narrative-preterite label is a form-class claim the pointed text does not carry, and no morphology layer is staged that could rescue it (the challenge's own account of where the wayyiqtol shape stands is narrower than the span's bytes). The commission reading it reaches for is nevertheless corroborated: כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י stands at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), distinguishing it from the public-oracle onsets. The splice asymmetry is real: the word-event at 13:8 is spliced at byte tier while the equally load-bearing onset at 13:3 is carried on the other witness's rendering alone. The one-unit result stands unchanged: the addressee never changes across 13:1-11, and the command, performance and interpretation phases of one enacted sign hold together absent an intervening seam of the ruled classes.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: qualify the scene clause -- name the time-and-place transition at 13:6 and state why it opens no ruled seam (same addressee, same enacted sign, no fresh commission to a new audience); replace the narrative-preterite label with a description the bytes support, namely the koh-amar shape standing in a private commission to the prophet rather than a public oracle onset, with its 3-verse book-wide sweep cited beside it; splice the word-event at oshb:Jer.13.3 at byte tier with its ref and tier named, matching the treatment of 13:8. Test the cure must pass: every form-class label is readable off the pointed bytes cited beside it, and every load-bearing device claim carries its own splice at a named tier.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on the command “Go, and buy yourself a linen belt” (web:Jer.13.1), a Yahweh-to-Jeremiah instruction fronted by כֹּֽה אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הָל֞וֹךְ (oshb:Jer.13.1, byte tier) -- the koh-amar shape used here as narrative preterite rather than a public oracle formula. A second word-event opens the burial command at 13:3 (‘the second time’), and the interpretation phase opens with its own word-event at 13:8, וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.13.8, byte tier). Command (13:1-2), the burial-and-recovery performance (13:3-7), and the interpretation (13:8-11, closing “the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah to cling to me”, web:Jer.13.11) stay one unit because no addressee or scene shift interrupts the sequence -- the scene keeps the same two participants, Jeremiah and the belt, from command to interpretation, and both internal word-event onsets mark phases of the same enacted sign rather than a fresh oracle to a new audience.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 13:3 and 13:8 as separate rows (one per word-event onset) was weighed and set aside: both introduce a phase of the same enacted sign rather than a change of addressee or scene, and a symbolic act's command, performance, and interpretation stay one unit unless a tier-1 seam of that kind intervenes.
current_row.literature_type_guess: enacted sign-act narrative: a worn-then-buried loincloth as a ruined emblem of covenant pride

docket.challenge_claim: That the form made to carry the opening seam recurs byte-identically one verse later inside the span, that its imperative label is not what the pointed bytes show, and that the closure warrant places a formula it never splices at a position the bytes contradict.
docket.grounds: Two arms hold as stated; one sub-claim needs correction. Recurrence: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם opens oshb:Jer.13.12 and the identical pointed run opens oshb:Jer.13.13 (both byte; that run at byte tier, sweep: 4 verses; the same shape at the consonantal tier, sweep: 18 verses), so the marker carrying the seam is not seam-exclusive and the in-span recurrence is undisclosed. That refines rather than kills the seam: what separates 13:12 from the belt's interpretation is a fresh commissioned saying to a broad audience after that interpretation closes, and the recurrence at 13:13 continues the same commissioned speech rather than opening a second unit. Form label: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם is a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation form, not a morphological imperative -- the imperatives in the neighbourhood are שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ at oshb:Jer.13.15, תְּנוּ֩ at oshb:Jer.13.16 and אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה at oshb:Jer.13.18 (all byte) -- so the label is a byte-checkable claim the text does not carry, though the clause does function as a commissioning frame. Closure position: at oshb:Jer.13.14 the formula נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה stands at the athnach with לֹֽא אֶחְמ֧וֹל and two further negated clauses running to the verse-final מֵהַשְׁחִיתָֽם (byte), so describing it as marking the unit's end misplaces it inside its verse; the closure reading itself survives, a fresh onset following at oshb:Jer.13.15 (sweep: 1 verse). Correction: the paragraph mark is NOT at the internal repetition point -- it is keyed to MT 13:12 while the repetition stands at 13:13; the row's paragraph disclosure for this span is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:12 and MT 13:14, single-witness, tier-3), and no variant note falls inside 13:12-13:14. The same misplacement of the closing formula is reproduced in the account that supports this row.
docket.remedy: boundary_rationale: describe the opening as a waw-prefixed suffix-conjugation commissioning clause rather than an imperative, and disclose that the identical pointed run opens 13:13 inside the span (with its byte-tier verse count), stating why the recurrence continues the commissioned speech instead of opening a second unit; restate the closure as the formula standing inside 13:14 with further clauses following it, corroborated by the fresh imperative onset at 13:15, not as a formula standing at the unit's end, and splice it at byte tier where it is asserted. If the re-description changes the driver, observed_substrate_signals, strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence re-open with it. Test the cure must pass: no form-class label stands that the pointed bytes contradict; any marker made to carry a seam is swept for in-span recurrence with the recurrence disclosed; and any position claim about a formula is read off that verse's own pointed bytes.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A fresh discourse-frame imperative opens the row: “Therefore you shall speak to them this word” (web:Jer.13.12), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.13.12, byte tier) -- Yahweh commissioning Jeremiah to relay a new saying, distinct from the belt's own interpretation just given. The commissioned proverb, “Every container should be filled with wine” (web:Jer.13.12), turns into a judgment against “the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.13), closing at 13:14 with the neum-YHWH formula marking the unit's end.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this proverb-oracle into the preceding sign-act row was considered: both concern the same belt-owning voice, but 13:12 opens its own commissioned-speech imperative rather than continuing the belt's interpretation, so the two stay separate.

docket.challenge_claim: That a variant note at 13:16 inside the span goes undisclosed even though the disclosure layer is engaged for the paragraph marks, and that a flock lexeme attested in 6 verses book-wide crosses the closing seam undisclosed.
docket.grounds: Both hold. oshb:Jer.13.16 stands inside the span and carries one note in the single-witness variant inventory; it is visible in the verse's own bytes as the unpointed ketiv ישית beside its pointed qere וְשִׁ֖ית (byte). The row's disclosure reaches only the paragraph marks at MT 13:14 and MT 13:17, so the disclosure set is incomplete on the book's largest single-witness variant layer at a verse inside the row's own span. Cohesion: עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה closes oshb:Jer.13.17, the row's own last verse, and the same lexeme returns as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (both byte; that consonantal form, sweep: 6 verses) -- a byte-true tie crossing this row's closing seam, undisclosed, arguing continuity against the cut until it is disclosed. The onset is sound and verified: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.13.15 and that imperative pair is unique in the book (sweep: 1 verse). The third arm is minor but right: declining the lament typing by appeal to which spans are enumerated is not a byte ground; the ground that does hold is וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ at oshb:Jer.13.17 (byte), whose second-person plural verb continues the plural audience addressed from 13:15.
docket.remedy: device_notes: add the single variant note at oshb:Jer.13.16 with its type and single-witness disclosure alongside the paragraph marks already carried; add the flock lexeme crossing the row's closing seam from 13:17 to 13:20 with its swept object and verse count, stating why the cut still holds against it. strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the refusal of the lament typing on the span's bytes -- the plural address running through 13:17 -- rather than on which spans are enumerated. Test the cure must pass: every variant note falling inside the span appears in the row's disclosure set; every device straddling the row's own seams is disclosed with object and count; and no rejection rests on an enumeration in place of the span's bytes.

current_row.boundary_rationale: “Hear, and give ear” (web:Jer.13.15), rendering שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ (oshb:Jer.13.15, byte tier), opens a fresh imperative address to the audience distinct from the commissioned proverb just closed. The call to give Yahweh glory before darkness falls (13:16) shifts in 13:17 into first-person prophetic grief -- “my soul will weep in secret for your pride” -- without any addressee or scene change, so the weeping stays inside this warning rather than opening a fresh unit.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Labeling this row lament_confession on the strength of 13:17's first-person weeping was considered and set aside: the enumerated confession and communal-lament spans do not include 13:17, and the weeping here sits inside a warning addressed outward to the audience rather than a petition addressed to Yahweh.

docket.challenge_claim: Both challenges land on one ground: the rejection of the one-poem rival rests on reading 13:20 as addressed to a second-feminine-singular figure, on one of the twelve doubled-note verses of the variant inventory, with that doubled note undisclosed. One adds that the plural forms opening the verse contradict the reading and that two byte-true ties bracket the two-verse span undisclosed.
docket.grounds: The same defect from both lenses, with a distinct second arm added by one of them; the defect is real and the stronger framing overstates it. oshb:Jer.13.20 carries two notes in the single-witness variant inventory -- a doubled-note verse -- and they sit on exactly the forms the rejection reads: the unpointed ketiv שאי and וראי stand in the verse bytes beside the pointed qere שְׂא֤וּ and וּרְא֔וּ (byte), whose plural endings are visible, and their object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (byte) carries a second-person masculine plural suffix under either reading (that imperative-plus-object pair, sweep: 1 verse). The row asserts a second-feminine-singular addressee there and discloses no note, on the largest single-witness variant layer in the book. The characterization is right about the verse's second half -- לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (byte) are feminine singular -- and wrong about its opening, which is where the rejection places the shift. Second arm, byte-true and undisclosed: תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם closes oshb:Jer.13.18 and recurs as תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (that consonantal form, sweep: 4 verses, three of them in this chapter), and עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה at oshb:Jer.13.17 recurs as הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ at oshb:Jer.13.20 (sweep: 6 verses) -- both tie this span to the material past its close and support the rival it sets aside. Framing correction: the seam is not falsified. The opening at oshb:Jer.13.18 is a morphological imperative, אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה (byte), naming a new addressee pair; the addressee does change at 13:20 under either reading of the doubled note; the paragraph disclosure for 13:18-19 is complete and correctly typed (setumah at MT 13:17 and MT 13:19, single-witness, tier-3) with no variant note inside the span; and the row already holds at reduced confidence with the frontier flag raised and concedes the rival's force. That places this at a ground-rewrite plus a mandatory disclosure, not at a falsified warrant.
docket.remedy: strongest_rejected_alternative: re-ground the closing seam on what 13:20 actually carries -- plural imperatives with a second-person masculine plural object opening the verse, and the feminine-singular address governing from mid-verse -- instead of an unqualified second-feminine-singular characterization; the corrected ground must hold under BOTH the ketiv and the qere. device_notes: disclose the doubled variant note at oshb:Jer.13.20 with both members named and single-witness disclosure, and disclose the two ties crossing the row's edges -- the glory-crown form recurring from 13:18 at 13:20, and the flock lexeme recurring from 13:17 at 13:20 -- each with swept object and verse count, stating why the cut holds against them. Keep the row's reduced confidence and frontier flag. Test the cure must pass: no form-class ground stands on a verse carrying a variant note unless that note is disclosed and both members are read; and every device straddling the row's edges is disclosed with object and count.

current_row.boundary_rationale: “Say to the king and to the queen mother” (web:Jer.13.18) opens on אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), a discourse imperative naming a new addressee pair -- the king and the queen mother -- distinct from the plural audience of 13:15-17. The two verses form one short oracle: the royal pair's fallen crown (13:18) and Judah's captivity (13:19) belong to the same announcement, with no further seam between them.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running 13:18-19 together with the material that follows through 13:27 as one royal-and-national poem was considered: the addressee shifts again at 13:20 to a second-feminine-singular Jerusalem figure, a distinct enough referent from the king and the queen mother to keep the two apart, though the case for reading it as one sustained poem is not without force.

docket.challenge_claim: One item: the row's observed_substrate_signals names a koh-amar speech formula that occurs nowhere within Jer.13.20-13.27, the seam and the typing being otherwise byte-sound. The converging item raises the same formula defect and three more: the opening seam's person-shift warrant is not delivered at the opening of 13:20, the woe-lexeme contrast carries a byte-false form label at 22:13 and 23:1, and two byte-true catchwords straddle the row's own opening seam undisclosed.
docket.grounds: The formula arm is the SAME defect in both items; the other three are distinct and additional. Formula (upheld): the census object koh amar YHWH returns 152 verses (sweep: 152 verses; with the single adonai-YHWH stack at 7:20 the census is 153), and its chapter-13 sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12 and 13:13 (sweep: 4 verses in the chapter), all standing before the span, the next site at 14:10 — none falls inside 13:20-13:27, so the declared signal has no support in the span's own bytes. The span's actual divine formula is נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.13.25, byte tier). Person shift (upheld): 13:20 opens שאי שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וראי וּרְא֔וּ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier for the pointed members; the two ketiv members stand unpointed in the source), a doubled-note verse in the single-witness inventory whose two notes sit on the two opening imperatives — feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere — with the intervening object עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) carrying a masculine-plural suffix under either reading. The feminine-singular forms לָ֔ךְ and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stand in the verse's second half, so the shift is not what 13:20 opens with. The run the row actually splices, הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier), is a definite masculine-plural participle with a prepositional phrase and carries no addressee marking at all, while the English paired with it, “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20), renders the contested imperatives that lie OUTSIDE the splice: gloss extent exceeds splice extent at exactly the point the warrant turns on. Recording the note as consulted but not spliced is a mark disclosure, not an answer to the reading it complicates. Form label (upheld): 22:13 and 23:1 each open on bare ה֣וֹי (oshb:Jer.22.13 and oshb:Jer.23.1, byte tier) as the verse's first token; the vav-prefixed shape וְה֥וֹי (oshb:Jer.34.5, byte tier) stands at two verses (sweep: 2 verses — 22:18 and 34:5), both funeral cries, so calling the 22:13 and 23:1 onsets vav-prefixed is contradicted by their own bytes. The oy digit is right: that lexeme is token-bound at 8 verses (sweep: 8 verses — 4:13, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 18:17, 30:14, 31:16, 48:46), against 14 for a bare consonantal substring (sweep: 14 verses). Cohesion (upheld): תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier) closes 13:18 and תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) closes 13:20, that stem standing at 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses — 13:11, 13:18, 13:20, 33:9); עֵ֥דֶר (oshb:Jer.13.17, byte tier) closes 13:17 and הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) stands inside 13:20, that noun at 6 verses (sweep: 6 verses — 6:3, 13:17, 13:20, 31:10, 31:24, 51:23). Both straddle the row's own opening seam, and conceding shared imagery in the rejected alternative is not disclosure of a byte-true device. The seam itself survives — the feminine-singular Jerusalem address does govern 13:20b through the explicit vocative at 13:27 — but the stated ground, the sole cited splice, one of the two declared signals and a named form class are all byte-defective. Parashah disclosure is accurate as written (setumah at 13:19 ahead of the opening, petuchah at 13:27 at the close; single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), and the span carries no paseq seg.
docket.remedy: No respan; the cut at 13:20 stands. (1) boundary_rationale: restate the opening ground where the bytes put it — 13:20 opens with the doubled-note imperative pair (feminine singular on the ketiv, masculine plural on the qere) and a masculine-plural object, and the feminine-singular address begins mid-verse at the 'to you' and 'your glory' forms and then governs through the vocative at 13:27; say that the note falls on the very forms the person reading turns on, rather than logging it as consulted-but-not-spliced. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the splice so the spliced extent covers exactly what the paired English renders, then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: strike 'vav-prefixed' from the woe contrast — 22:13 and 23:1 open on bare hoy as their first token, and the vav-prefixed shape stands at 22:18 and 34:5 (sweep: 2 verses), both funeral cries. (4) observed_substrate_signals: remove speech_formula.koh_amar (no koh-amar verse falls in 13:20-13:27; the chapter's four sites are 13:1, 13:9, 13:12, 13:13); if a divine-formula signal is wanted the span's token is the neum-YHWH at 13:25. (5) device_notes or strongest_rejected_alternative: disclose and answer the two straddling catchwords with their swept objects and digits (the glory stem, sweep: 4 verses; the flock noun, sweep: 6 verses). (6) The signal field is dependent on the driver, so striking one entry re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative and confidence. TEST the cure must pass: no koh-amar verse inside the span on the named census object; every form-class label re-read off the pointed bytes at its own site; each straddling device named with object and digit; splice extent equal to gloss extent on every pairing.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The address turns to a second-feminine-singular figure at 13:20 -- “Lift up your eyes, and see those who come from the north” (web:Jer.13.20) renders הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן (oshb:Jer.13.20, byte tier) -- distinct from the king-and-queen-mother pair just addressed. (13:20 also carries a doubled ketiv/qere note on its two opening imperatives, consulted but not spliced here.) The sustained indictment of Jerusalem-as-woman runs through the scattering sentence (13:24-25) and the uncovering of her skirts (13:26) to the closing apostrophe: “Woe to you, Jerusalem” (web:Jer.13.27), where א֥וֹי לָךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Jer.13.27, byte tier) is the oy lexeme (sweep: 8 verses book-wide) -- a different word from the vav-prefixed hoy that opens the woe oracles at 22:13 and 23:1, so this row is not typed woe_oracle.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Joining 13:20-27 to the preceding royal oracle (13:18-19) into one ten-verse row was considered: the shift from a plural/2ms royal address to a sustained 2fs Jerusalem address is real, but the two share the same humiliation-and-exposure imagery, so the fold-together reading is not unreasonable.

docket.challenge_claim: The topical-header claim is byte-sound, but a ketiv/qere note inside the span goes undisclosed while the row makes a positive absence statement for the parashah layer; secondarily, the appeal to how header-bounded units elsewhere carry their attached content as one piece is uneven across the four attested sites.
docket.grounds: Upheld on the bytes, with one finding added. Disclosure: 14:3, inside the span, carries one note in the single-witness inventory and it stands in the verse as unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere, צעוריהם צְעִירֵיהֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.14.3, byte tier for the pointed member). The row's device_notes state positively that no verse within 14:1-14:6 carries a parashah mark — true on the inventory, as is the petuchah at 13:27 ahead of the row — so one single-witness layer is engaged with a positive absence claim while a present item in the other, the largest such inventory in this book (141 notes over 124 verses), goes unmentioned; that asymmetry is what the span-relevant disclosure rule exists to catch. The header object and digit are sound and are NOT disturbed: the shape carrying the prophet's name returns 14:1, 46:1, 47:1 and 49:34 (sweep: 4 verses), and dropping the name widens the result to five by admitting the to-him variant in the superscription at 1:2 (sweep: 5 verses), so the needle is correctly bounded and not blended with the eleven-verse prose-sermon shape. Secondary arm upheld: 46:1 reads “Yahweh’s word which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.” (web:Jer.46.1) and heads the whole nations collection rather than bundling an attached description, while 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles each with its own attached setting — the cross-site analogy needs a per-site read. NEW FINDING, raised by neither item: gloss extent and splice extent come apart in the same sentence. The splice ends at דִּבְרֵ֖י (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) while the English paired with it, “This is Yahweh’s word that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought” (web:Jer.14.1), renders הַבַּצָּרֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.14.1, byte tier) as well — one token past the spliced extent. The span carries no paseq seg, so nothing is owed there.
docket.remedy: No respan; the header seam and the 4-verse digit stand. (1) device_notes: add the ketiv/qere note at 14:3 (single-witness), stated as its own layer and kept distinct from the parashah sentence, which is accurate and stays as written. (2) boundary_rationale: re-cut the header splice so it ends where the paired English ends — extend the splice through the drought noun or trim the English to stop before it — then re-collate at byte tier. (3) boundary_rationale: replace the blanket cross-site analogy with a per-site statement (46:1 heads the nations collection rather than bundling a description; 47:1 and 49:34 head single-nation oracles with their own attached settings), or drop the analogy and rest the bundling on the span's own absence of an addressee or scene shift through 14:6. The defect is therefore one sentence's category conflation, not a frame-owner error. The boundary is not disturbed, and the span's disclosure is in fact complete: setumah at 14:9 ahead of the row and setumah at 14:10 itself (single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets), with no ketiv/qere note and no paseq seg on 14:10.

docket.challenge_claim: The seam driver is a form-class misidentification — the opening word of 14:17 is a waw-consecutive perfect, not an imperative — and the same construction runs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force.
docket.grounds: Upheld on the pointed bytes, and it bites harder than the item frames it. Form class: 14:17 opens וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) — vav with sheva, alef with qamats, mem with patah, resh with sheva, and a final tav carrying dagesh and qamats, the second-masculine-singular suffix-conjugation ending. The form is waw plus perfect, not a morphological imperative. The second-masculine-singular imperative of this verb stands three verses earlier at 13:18, אֱמֹ֥ר (oshb:Jer.13.18, byte tier), with no such ending, and the discourse-frame imperative class that may drive a seam is instanced by true plural imperatives at 4:5 and 10:1. No morphology layer is staged, so this is argued from the pointing plus both witnesses' renderings, which read a modal continuation rather than a command. The weight: the row asserts the class in boundary_rationale AND carries speech_formula.discourse_imperative as its single declared substrate signal, so the mislabel leaves the row with no sound declared driver, and that field is dependent on the driver. Not seam-exclusive: the construction וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֲלֵיהֶם֙ (oshb:Jer.14.17, byte tier) returns 18 verses (sweep: 18 verses — 5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) and the bare form 30 verses (sweep: 30 verses); at 15:2 it sits mid-verse inside a conditional as an ordinary continuation, וְאָמַרְתָּ֨ אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם (oshb:Jer.15.2, byte tier), four verses on in the same stretch. What does NOT follow is a respan: reading 14:17 as mere continuation of the divine speech begun at 14:14 is a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, and the cut is re-groundable without one — 14:14-16 is divine speech to the prophet ABOUT the prophets and the people, while 14:17 commissions a word for delivery TO them, and both witnesses open a fresh quoted message there. The item is also right that 14:16, just ahead of the opening, carries no parashah mark, so no tier-3 corroboration is available at this seam. NEW FINDING: the same construction stands verse-initially at 13:12 and again at 13:13, adjacent verses in the same stretch and both inside the 18-verse set, so the mislabel class reaches past this row.
docket.remedy: No respan. (1) observed_substrate_signals: replace speech_formula.discourse_imperative — the form is a waw-prefixed second-masculine-singular suffix conjugation, not an imperative — with a dotted key matching what the bytes carry (a speech-delivery command opening a fresh quoted message, or the change in who the message is addressed to across 14:16 into 14:17). (2) boundary_rationale: strike 'A fresh discourse-frame imperative opens the row'; state the form as the pointed bytes carry it and re-ground the seam on the delivery command plus the addressee change, and disclose that the same construction recurs mid-verse at 15:2 with no boundary force and is attested at 18 verses book-wide (sweep: 18 verses), so it is not seam-exclusive. (3) Dependent fields: this is the row's single declared signal, so its replacement re-opens strongest_rejected_alternative, unit_type and confidence. (4) device_notes: state plainly that 14:16 carries no parashah mark, so this seam has no tier-3 corroboration, rather than leaving it implied. (5) CORPUS-WIDE ORDER, carried as its own sweep and not folded into this row's fix: sweep all 18 sites of the delivery construction (5:19, 7:28, 8:4, 11:3, 13:12, 13:13, 14:17, 15:2, 16:11, 17:20, 19:11, 23:33, 25:27, 25:28, 25:30, 26:4, 38:26, 43:10) plus the 30-verse bare set, and correct every row that labels this waw-perfect an imperative or a discourse-frame imperative, or that rests a seam on its supposed exclusivity — the verse-initial occurrences at 13:12 and 13:13 are the nearest instances. TEST the cure must pass: every form-class label re-read off the pointed bytes at its own site, with the imperative at 13:18 as the contrasting control; no seam-exclusivity claim for a construction whose sweep digit and site list are not stated beside it.

The mark arm verifies as well: two variant notes fall inside Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21, at MT 15:11 -- שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), the verse cited as the reply's onset -- and at MT 15:16, inside the complaint; neither is disclosed. Independently re-verified and NOT defective: the row's 8-verse digit for the alef-initial outcry lexeme matches the byte-derived count object exactly (8 verses, MT keys), while a bare consonantal substring sweep on the same three letters returns 14 verses, contaminated by the enemy and fool bases -- the digit is true only under the token-bound object the row names, and it names it. B2-2.docket_item: Split P05-014 (Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21) at 15:19 into complaint and second divine reply?
B2-2.grounds: The challenge is byte-confirmed and the row's stated hold-together ground is byte-false. MT 15:11 opens the reply on a bare אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), which is neither one of the three word-event shapes nor a koh-amar; MT 15:15 turns to the prophet's own mouth, אַתָּ֧ה יָדַ֣עְתָּ יְהוָ֗ה זָכְרֵ֤נִי וּפָקְדֵ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier); the first-person complaint holds through 15:16-15:18; and לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) therefore does change the speaking mouth. So 15:19 IS a licensed tier-1 seam and the row's reason for declining it is contradicted by the bytes it cites. Licensed is not compelled. The span is one exchange with one participant set: the adversaries answered at 15:20 are the people already standing at כֻּלֹּ֥ה מְקַלְלַֽונִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) and מֵרֹ֣דְפַ֔י (oshb:Jer.15.15, byte tier), and 15:19-15:21 introduces no participant, addressee pair or scene that 15:10-15:18 does not already carry. That is what separates this seam from the two seams the corpus does cut in the same frame, where a named opponent set enters at MT 11:21 and the prophet's own brothers and father's house enter at MT 12:6. Cutting here would separate a reply from the complaint it answers on a seam that adds no participant, which is the over-split direction, and the confessions' speaker-frame edges are a held-open low-confidence region where honest reduced confidence, not a respan, is the disposition. Disclosure re-verified against the inventory: exactly two variant notes fall inside Jer.15.10-Jer.15.21, at MT 15:11, visible in the bytes as שרותך שֵֽׁרִיתִ֖יךָ (oshb:Jer.15.11, byte tier), and at MT 15:16, דבריך דְבָֽרְךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.15.16, byte tier); neither is disclosed. The parashah disclosure is complete and correctly typed, setumah at MT 15:10, 15:14, 15:16, 15:17 and 15:18 with a petuchah at MT 15:21, single-witness and tier-3 weak. COUNT OBJECT named for the outcry digit the row carries: the attested pointed form אֽוֹי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) returns 3 verses at byte and accent-stripped tiers (MT 4:31, 15:10, 45:3), and the bare consonantal substring returns 14 verses, blended with the enemy and fool bases and with the royal name at MT 52:31, so the row's 8-verse figure is a lexeme-level object distinct from both staged digits and true only under the object the row names, which it does name. Carried as a disclosure requirement, not as a defect finding.

current_row.boundary_rationale: “Woe is me, my mother” (web:Jer.15.10) opens אֽוֹי לִ֣י אִמִּ֔י כִּ֣י יְלִדְתִּ֗נִי (oshb:Jer.15.10, byte tier) -- another oy apostrophe (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, the same lexeme spliced at 13:27 above), here turned inward as Jeremiah's own outcry rather than a judgment against the city, a clean scene shift from the divine judgment speech just closed. Yahweh's reply opens at 15:11 without a further addressee change (private dialogue continues), and a second reply opens “Therefore Yahweh says” (web:Jer.15.19) on לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.15.19, byte tier) -- a koh-amar with no change of frame-owner, so it does not itself open a fresh row. Complaint and reply run together to the closing promise of deliverance at 15:21.
